explainTr: Modallerden sonra her zaman yalın fiil gelir. Zorunluluk: must / have to. Yasak: mustn't. Gerek yok: don't have to / needn't. Tavsiye: should / ought to. İzin ve rica: can, could, may. Olasılık: must (kesin), might / may / could (belki), can't (imkânsız).

Geçmiş için modal + have + V3 kullanılır. Çıkarım: must have left (kesin ayrıldı), can't have left (ayrılmış olamaz), might have left (belki ayrıldı). Pişmanlık/eleştiri: should have called (aramalıydı). Gereksiz iş: needn't have hurried (acele etmeseydin de olurdu).
En sık karışan çift: mustn't ve don't have to. 'You mustn't run' koşmak yasak demektir; 'You don't have to run' koşman şart değil demektir.
grammar.compareTr: Türkçede 'gitmeli', 'gitmek zorunda', 'gitmeyebilir' farklı eklerle verilir. İngilizcede ayrı kelimeler var ve zamanı have + V3 taşır: 'Gitmeliydin' = You should have gone.

reading.title: Safety first at orientation
reading.text:
On Friday afternoon, Hafsa attended an orientation for new substitutes at Jefferson Elementary. The assistant principal, Mr. Collins, began with a simple sentence: "You must never leave a classroom unsupervised." He explained that this rule is essential because children can get hurt in a minute.

Next, he talked about phones. "You may use your phone for emergencies, but you shouldn't check messages while teaching," he said. "Students notice everything." A teacher in the back asked whether substitutes could take photos of the class. Mr. Collins shook his head. "No. You mustn't post or share any photos. That would violate district policy."

Mr. Collins also reminded them of what they don't have to do. "You don't have to grade tests unless the sub plan says so, and you needn't stay after four o'clock. But if you notice a safety problem, you ought to report it immediately." He gave an example from last winter. A substitute had seen a wet floor near the gym, but she hadn't told anyone. A student slipped and broke his wrist. "She should have called the office," he said quietly. "It might have prevented the accident."

Hafsa listened carefully and wrote everything in her notebook. During the break, she talked to a young teacher named Ms. Chen. "I was so nervous in my first week," Ms. Chen admitted. "I couldn't remember anything. I must have looked terrible." Hafsa laughed. "I'm sure you looked fine. I think being nervous is normal."

At the end, Mr. Collins handed out a card with emergency numbers. "Keep it in your pocket. You can't be too careful," he said. As Hafsa walked to the bus stop, she felt both tired and proud. She knew that she could not remember every rule yet, but she could always ask for help. "That is what colleagues are for," she thought.

writing.promptEn: Write an advice note (120-180 words) to a new substitute teacher. Use must, mustn't, don't have to, should and should have.
frames: If I were you, I would ...
On my first day, I should have ...
writing.model:
Dear new colleague,

Congratulations on your new job! I would like to share a few tips from my first weeks. First of all, you must always follow the sub plan. The regular teacher has prepared it carefully, and the students will feel more comfortable if the day looks familiar.

You mustn't leave the classroom unsupervised, even for a minute. If you need help, call the front office. You also mustn't share photos of students, because it violates district policy. You don't have to grade the tests unless the plan says so, and you needn't stay after the last bell.

You should arrive at least twenty minutes early. On my first day, I came late, and I should have checked the plan before the students arrived. It made my morning much harder. If I were you, I would also learn the names of two or three students quickly, because names help you build respect.

Most importantly, you can always ask Mr. Brown for help. Good luck!

Hafsa
